metadata.summary: Oncofetal programs are often co-opted in high-grade gliomas and represent tumor cell vulnerabilities for therapeutic exploitation. Here, we integrate single nucleus RNA-seq and single-cell ATAC sequencing data generated from germinal matrix and cortical plate regions macrodissected from prenatal and postnatal developing brain autopsy tissue, creating an expanded spatiotemporal multi-omic dataset of gliogenic progenitors. The integrated multi-omics data includes previously published data (Ramos et al, Nature Commun 2022; Herring et al, Cell 2022) as well as newly-generated and herein deposited data. We use this dataset to interrogate oncofetal cell state composition in grade 4 gliomas across several published high-grade glioma / glioblastoma (GBM) datasets to uniquely assess tumor heterogeneity related to infiltrative biology near the margin and disease recurrence, in addition to genomic drivers. Our analyses reveal the preferential enrichment of glial intermediate progenitor cell (gIPC)-like cell state in GBM, most reminiscent of third-trimester germinal matrix gIPC progenitors, across tumor regions and in recurrence, irrespective of EGFR amplification status.

metadata.summary: Microexons are extremely short exons that are highly conserved in vertebrates and are essential for normal brain development. Their small size poses a challenge for canonical exon-definition splice site recognition, which typically relies on spliceosomal interactions across standard length exons. Here, we determine the sequence and RNA structural features of neural microexons in humans in comparison with chickens. We find that neural microexons share intronic features that extend the functional distance between the branchpoint and the 3’ splice site, including distal positioning and lengthening of polypyrimidine tracts. Using experimental RNA structure-probing on a subset of neural microexons, we show that the branchpoint-to-splice site region is unusually accessible and relatively unpaired compared to other exon classes. However, we find little support for shared RNA secondary structures between orthologous human and chicken precursor RNAs despite high sequence conservation. Using the chick embryo as a developmental model, we demonstrate that a subset of neural microexons undergo dynamic, stage-specific regulation during brain development that correlates with expression of known microexon regulators, SRRM4 and NOVA1. Our data suggest that neural microexon splicing fluctuates during brain development and may rely on an extended polypyrimidine tract and structural accessibility for splicing efficiency, rather than conserved secondary structures.

metadata.summary: Direct cardiac reprogramming relies on a combination of canonical cardiac transcription factors, typically consisting of Mef2c, Gata4, and Tbx5 (MGT). However, successful lineage conversion requires additional endogenous factors that coordinate the chromatin and transcriptional changes underlying fibroblast-to-cardiomyocyte conversion. Here, we identify Activating Transcription Factor 7 (Atf7) as a critical supporting factor that enables efficient direct cardiac reprogramming. Loss of function studies in primary murine cardiac fibroblasts demonstrate that Atf7 knockdown markedly reduces MGT mediated reprogramming efficiency, with the strongest impairment occurring when Atf7 is depleted during the early priming window of days 0–3. Transcriptomic profiling reveals that Atf7 knockdown disrupts the induction of cardiomyocyte gene programs while derepressing fibroblast  and extracellular matrix–associated pathways, shifting the global expression profile toward a non reprogrammed state. These findings support a bifunctional regulatory role of Atf7 in promoting cardiomyocyte-specific gene activation while repressing fibroblast-associated transcriptional networks.

metadata.summary: Myocardial infarction (MI) causes cardiomyocyte loss and fibrotic scar formation, disrupting electrical communication and impairing cardiac function. Conductive hydrogels have been studied to reconstruct an electroactive microenvironment for the infarcted myocardium, yet their regenerative effect is limited by the impaired function of surviving cardiomyocytes. Here, we developed a mechanoelectrically active and paintable hydrogel capable of converting cardiac motion into localized electrical stimulation to repair infarcted myocardium. The paintable nature of the hydrogel enables easy application onto irregular epicardial surfaces using a customized brush, while subsequent photocrosslinking allows selective adhesion of the hydrogel to only epicardial surfaces, not to surrounding tissues. Under cyclic loading and in contracting cardiac organoids, the hydrogel generated physiologically relevant electrical potentials, demonstrating efficient deformation-induced charge generation. In a rat MI model, the hydrogel providing electrostimulation alleviated ventricular wall thinning and fibrosis, promoted neovascularization and M2 macrophage polarization, and improved cardiac function. Transcriptomic analysis further revealed upregulation of genes involved in myocardial contraction and energy metabolism. As such, our study offers a minimally invasive and clinically translatable approach for cardiac repair and other tissue applications.

observations.text: Title and abstract screening is among the most labor-intensive steps of systematic reviews. Jev, a low-cost AI decision model, scores records against eligibility criteria without screening labels. We scored 169,982 records from 128 reviews and, after tuning on development reviews, evaluated 23 held-out reviews once and 31 Cochrane reviews post hoc. Jev outranked the best free ranker in all 23 held-out reviews (mean AUC 0.966 vs 0.831) and came within 0.011 AUC of Claude Opus 5.5 on 1999 records at about 1/700 of its list-price cost (US$0.02/1000 records). Combined with active learning, it raised work saved at 95% recall from 0.659 to 0.806. A fixed score threshold fell below 95% recall in 3 of 28 Cochrane reviews, whereas Jev ranking with statistical stopping (post hoc) reached 95% recall in all 51 reviews, reading 86-88% of records. Label-free ranking with Jev was accurate and inexpensive, but stopping safely required screening decisions.
observations.title: Label-free, low-cost AI ranking for systematic review screening

BackgroundIn people with type 2 diabetes (T2D), postprandial glucose weighs on glycaemic control, and carbohydrate counting is difficult. Patients can describe their meal but rarely quantify it.

ObjectiveTo assess (1) whether a small open large language model (LLM), fine-tuned on public data, estimates the carbohydrate content of a meal described in words, and (2) what this carbohydrate adds to the prediction of the postprandial glucose rise in two public cohorts.

MethodsStep 1: the Qwen3-4B LLM was fine-tuned with QLoRA on Nutrition5k dishes and compared with an automatically matched USDA food composition table and with Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B used without training, on test dishes (internal control) and on 100 real meals of ShanghaiT2DM patients, whose reference carbohydrate was computed from the recorded quantities. Step 2: the maximum glucose rise between 0 and 120 minutes ({Delta}Gmax) was predicted by personalised gradient boosting (M2), compared with a spline linear regression and with the Chronos-2 foundation model, using only information available at meal start and person-level cross-validation, in ShanghaiT2DM (people with T2D recruited in two Shanghai hospitals; carbohydrate estimated by the LLM) and CGMacros (free-living adults in Santa Barbara, California; carbohydrate entered in the dataset, no text). Step 3: the model was transferred between datasets. 95% confidence intervals (CI) were obtained by cluster BCa bootstrap (2,000 resamples).

ResultsOn the 100 real meals, the carbohydrate mean absolute error (MAE) of the fine-tuned model was 12.2 [9.9, 15.2] g, almost half that of the table (22.6 g; paired difference -10.5 [-16.8, -6.0] g) and nearly a third of that of the same model without fine-tuning (34.3 g), with a bias of -10.3 g; on test dishes it was 2.2 [2.0, 2.5] g. Personalised gradient boosting (M2) reached a correlation between predicted and observed rises of r = 0.63 [0.55, 0.69] in CGMacros (1,286 meals, 45 adults) and 0.49 [0.42, 0.54] in ShanghaiT2DM (2,339 meals, 99 people with T2D), about twice the linear reference (r = 0.32 and 0.23); for a rise above 50 mg/dL, its area under the ROC curve (AUROC) was 0.80 and 0.74, versus 0.64 and 0.68 with pre-meal glucose alone. Adding carbohydrate to pre-meal glucose changed r by 0.095 [0.068, 0.128] in CGMacros and by 0.004 [-0.010, 0.017] in ShanghaiT2DM; difference between datasets: 0.091 [0.060, 0.126]. Applied from one dataset to the other, the model lost correlation ({Delta}r = -0.11 [-0.17, -0.05] towards ShanghaiT2DM and -0.12 [-0.19, -0.04] towards CGMacros). The full "text [->] LLM [->] glucose" chain was evaluated in ShanghaiT2DM only.

ConclusionAn open 4-billion-parameter LLM, fine-tuned with QLoRA on public data and usable offline, almost halves the error of carbohydrate counting for real meals described in words compared with an automatically matched table, with an underestimation of large meals. Personalised gradient boosting, based on pre-meal glucose and the persons usual response, doubles the correlation of a linear reference for predicting the glucose rise in both cohorts. Carbohydrate improved this prediction in CGMacros but not in ShanghaiT2DM; the two datasets differ in many respects, and the cause of this gap is not established.

observations.text: Enzyme catalyzed reactions drive metabolism and enable diverse applications in biotechnology and sustainable synthesis, but assigning catalytic functions to uncharacterized enzymes and finding enzymes for target reactions remain major challenges. Despite recent advances in machine learning, translating enzyme function prediction into systematic discovery across the vast space of uncharacterized proteins and biochemical reactions remains challenging. Here we present EzHit, a lightweight framework for bidirectional enzyme reaction retrieval. Across enzyme annotation, orphan-reaction retrieval and family-specific fine-tuning benchmarks, EzHit achieved strong top-ranked performance and outperformed representative enzyme reaction matching baselines. We further show that Mahalanobis distance based geometric confidence provides more useful reliability estimates than probability-derived uncertainty metrics or evidential learning, enabling confidence-aware prioritization of high scoring candidates. Owing to its efficiency, EzHit was applied to a nearly trillion-scale OMG_Prot50 with RHEA screen, yielding 8.20 billion retained enzyme reaction associations across 30.27 million predicted enzyme sequences. Experimental validation further confirmed the activity of EzHit prioritized metagenomic enzyme candidates for a sparsely annotated reaction. Together, these results establish EzHit as a scalable framework for enzyme annotation, reaction-guided mining and biocatalyst discovery

metadata.summary: Non-infectious granulomatous diseases, including sarcoidosis, lack targeted, steroid-sparing therapies to disrupt the persistent immune cell aggregates that drive chronic tissue morbidity. Integrating multi-organ single-cell RNA sequencing with spatial transcriptomics, we identify conserved macrophage-specific induction of osteopontin (OPN) across human skin, lung, and heart lesions. Mechanistically, we show that local tissue coagulation acts as a functional checkpoint, where proteolytic cleavage of OPN by tissue thrombin generates OPN fragments that activate macrophages through α4 integrin, which amplifies macrophage OPN expression and establishes a feed-forward circuit that sustains granuloma stability. In mouse models, genetic or pharmacologic disruption of this coagulation-immune axis, including the repurposed direct thrombin inhibitor dabigatran and thrombin cleavage-blocking OPN antibodies, reduces granuloma formation and promotes resolution of established chronic lesions. Together, these findings identify a thrombin-dependent feed-forward coagulation–immune circuit that maintains granuloma stability and provides multiple therapeutically actionable targets for non-infectious granulomatous disease.

metadata.summary: Truncating variants in desmoplakin (DSP) are a leading cause of arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy, a severe heart muscle disease characterized by fibrosis and life-threatening arrhythmias. Desmoplakin anchors the junctions that hold heart muscle cells together to the internal cytoskeleton, enabling the heart to withstand the force of each contraction. No targeted therapy exists, and DSP is too large for conventional gene replacement. Here we show, in explanted human hearts and in human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes, that truncating DSP variants reduce desmoplakin RNA and protein, and that the resulting haploinsufficiency renders cardiomyocytes vulnerable to cell–cell adhesion failure under contractile stress, preceded by disruption of the cell membrane. Lowering contractile force with the myosin inhibitor mavacamten prevents this failure. Circumventing the size of DSP, CRISPR-based transcriptional activation of the endogenous gene restores desmoplakin expression and rescues adhesion. Haploinsufficiency is therefore the primary defect in DSP cardiomyopathy, and transcriptional activation offers a therapeutic strategy.

metadata.summary: Myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury triggers the recruitment of inflammatory cells, including neutrophils and monocytes. Currently, effective treatment strategies are not available for this widely occurring harmful condition. Using metabololipidomics, we uncovered relative reductions in the pro-resolving lipid mediator Resolvin-D1 (RvD1) early after reperfusion in both mouse and human transplanted hearts, and that exogenous treatment led to elevated tissue levels of RvD1. By intravital two-photon microscopy, we discovered that that pre-operative instillation of RvD1 into the donor heart or peri-operative systemic recipient RvD1 treatment reduced recruitment of neutrophils. Mechanistically, we found that RvD1 provides protection by signaling through Alx/Fpr2 on donor monocytes, which reduces their production of IL-1b, attenuating intravascular neutrophil aggregation and extravasation.  After allogeneic transplantation, peri-operative RvD1 treatment reduces myeloid cell recruitment, abrogates macrophage pro-inflammatory signaling within cardiac allografts, and significantly prolongs graft survival. This study defines the mechanistic basis of a therapeutic strategy that modulates inflammatory responses during myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury and provides a platform for the design of clinical trials.

observations.text:
BACKGROUNDThe chromosome 9p21.3 locus is among the strongest genetic risk loci for cardiovascular disease (CVD), yet the regulatory mechanisms underlying this association remain poorly understood. Previous vascular disease studies focused predominantly on the role of this locus in smooth muscle cell (SMC) dysfunction, whereas its potential role in endothelial cells (ECs) remains less well characterized. Here, we sought to identify candidate regulatory variants at 9p21.3, their distal target genes, and effector transcripts that contribute to CVD-related phenotypes in ECs.

METHODSPromoter capture Hi-C was used to map chromatin interactions at 9p21.3 in primary human ascending aortic SMCs (n=6), supplementing the previously obtained ECs (n=16) dataset. To support the regulatory relevance of these interactions, expression quantitative trait locus analysis was performed in 136 vascular biopsies. Variant effects were prioritized in silico using AlphaGenome. The regulatory activity of the prioritized region was validated using CRISPR activation.

RESULTSChromatin interaction mapping identified a complex regulatory architecture at the 9p21.3 locus involving 19 putative regulatory elements and 15 genes across ECs and SMCs. MIR31HG showed the most recurrent distal promoter connectivity with the 9p21.3 region. Consistent with the chromatin interaction map, expression of MIR31HG transcripts was associated with genetic variation at the 9p21.3 locus. In ECs, the lncRNA MIR31HG, but not miR-31, was responsive to hemodynamic flow. Depletion of MIR31HG in ECs was associated with endothelial activation. Epigenetic tracks and deep learning predictions highlighted an active enhancer element at 9p21.3, which was subsequently validated by CRISPR activation and increased MIR31HG expression, confirming its capacity to regulate MIR31HG over a large genomic distance of approximately 538 kb.

CONCLUSIONSAltogether, these data implicate lncRNA MIR31HG as a likely effector of the 9p21.3 CVD locus, linking the cis-regulatory element and heritable genetic variation in the respective region to endothelial activation through long-range enhancer regulation.

metadata.summary: Diabetic cardiomyopathy is a clinical condition of ventricular dysfunction, with obesity and insulin resistance as the primary risk factors. Under this condition, the heart accumulates fatty acids and encounters lipotoxicity, which impairs cardiac insulin sensitivity and leads to cardiomyopathy. Angiotensin-(1-9) is a peptide of the counter-regulatory axis of the renin-angiotensin system with cardioprotective effects in myocardial infarction. However, its role in diabetic cardiomyopathy is unknown. To explore the role of angiotensin-(1-9), we first induced lipotoxic stress in the heart by high-fat diet (HFD) feeding in mice. Angiotensin-(1-9) was then administered for four weeks using osmotic mini-pumps. Cardiac function was assessed by, and insulin sensitivity was evaluated in tissues after a bolus of insulin injection. Moreover, lipotoxic stress in vitro was modeled by high glucose medium plus palmitate in neonatal rat ventricular myocytes (NRVMs). We show that angiotensin-(1-9) improves myocardial function and reverts pathological cardiac remodeling in mice. Moreover, angiotensin-(1-9) enhances whole-body glucose tolerance and reduces homeostatic model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR). We next demonstrate that angiotensin-(1-9) increases insulin sensitivity in the heart and skeletal muscle but not in adipose tissue or the liver. Mechanistically, angiotensin-(1-9) does not affect insulin signaling in cardiomyocytes at baseline, while it significantly improves insulin action under lipotoxic stress through AT2 receptor (AT2R) and PKA. These findings demonstrate that angiotensin-(1-9) improves cardiac function under metabolic challenge and promotes insulin signaling in cardiomyocytes under lipotoxicity, which may shed light on the therapeutic exploration against diabetic cardiomyopathy.

IntroductionThis study aimed to characterize the neurochemical profile of Alzheimers disease (AD) continuum stages using proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy (1H-MRS) data for brain metabolites and macromolecules. We used Orthogonal Projection to Latent Structures Discriminant Analysis (OPLS-DA) to classify diagnostic groups and assess feature importance.

MethodsOur dataset consisted of 7 T short-echo time 1H-MRS spectra of the posterior cingulate cortex/precuneus of individuals diagnosed with AD (n = 27) or Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI, n = 27) and Healthy Controls (HC, n = 31). Classification used 100-round Monte Carlo cross-validation based on metabolite concentrations and macromolecular peak intensities. Variable importance in projection (VIP) was assessed across classification models to identify the most relevant neurochemical features. The resulting metabolite rankings were compared with previous literature to evaluate their biological plausibility.

ResultsClassification was strongest for AD versus HC (AUC=0.88) and lower for comparisons involving MCI. Metabolites contributing most strongly to classification included myo-inositol, ascorbate, and choline-containing compounds, consistent with previous studies on AD-related neurochemical alterations. In addition, specific macromolecular components were identified as relevant features, suggesting a potential contribution of MM signals to the characterization of AD-related neurochemistry.

DiscussionThese findings support the use of short-echo-time 1H-MRS as a complementary tool for characterizing neurochemical changes in the AD continuum, with potential applications in disease characterization and monitoring, warranting validation in larger cohorts.

observations.text: The role of Rapid Eye Movement (REM) sleep in memory consolidation remains poorly understood. Several influential ideas propose that REM sleep serves to eliminate crosstalk between memories, thereby orthogonalizing representations of similar ones; however, mechanistic confirmation remains sparse. Here we used recurrent neural networks trained with Equilibrium Propagation (EP), a biologically plausible training algorithm, to investigate the role of REM-like sleep in memory consolidation. We found that REM-like sleep reduces memory interference by decorrelating task-specific neuronal populations, isolating individual memory traces. During sleep, reactivation was dominated by the population encoding the most recent memory, which had taken over the inputs of older memories during new learning. The excitation/inhibition balance of inputs onto this population shifted toward inhibition, most strongly from older-memory populations, so that older memories again activated their own neurons. Spreading the same total synaptic change evenly across all target populations abolished this recovery. We call this mechanism reactivation-targeted pruning: synaptic weights onto the reactivated population decrease when its neurons fire while their presynaptic partners are silent. The mechanism held under a synapse-level Dale's law, and excitatory plasticity alone, with inhibitory synapses fixed, was sufficient. These findings suggest mechanistic principles underlying REM sleep's role in memory consolidation.
observations.title: Firing Without Wiring: How REM-like Sleep Reactivation Rebalances Excitation and Inhibition to Orthogonalize Memories

PurposeTo evaluate whether visually assessed high-quality prostate MRI, as defined by the Prostate Imaging Quality (PI-QUAL) scoring system, is sufficient to ensure consistent AI model performance, or whether hidden acquisition-related technical effects introduce variability that cannot be detected through visual inspection.

MethodsThis retrospective study included 568 bpMRI scans from seven institutions, classified using PI-QUAL v2 into high-quality (scores 2-3) and low-quality (score 1) groups. Quantitative image quality features were extracted using MRQy from T2w and ADC sequences. Three experiments were conducted on high-quality scans: (1) unsupervised clustering to identify hidden technical batch effects; (2) V-Net models (M) for prostate capsule segmentation on T2w using single-cluster and balanced multi-cluster training strategies; and (3) VoxelMorph-based deformable registration (M2) to align ADC maps to T2w images. Performance metrics included DSC, precision, recall, volume ratio, HD95, ASSD, and TRE. Kruskal-Wallis tests assessed cross-cluster variability, Two One-Sided Tests (TOST) evaluated performance equivalence, and bootstrap resampling quantified training efficiency.

ResultsClustering identified four clusters among 277 high-quality bpMRI scans. Single-cluster models showed variable performance (DSC=0.41-0.85) with significant batch effects (p<0.001), even with 140 training samples. The balanced multi-cluster model (n=60) eliminated batch effects (p=0.075), achieved equivalent performance (p<0.001), and demonstrated 2.23-fold greater training efficiency despite using 2.3-fold fewer samples. Registration performance also varied significantly across clusters (TRE=0.86-5.47 mm, p<0.001).

ConclusionAcquisition-related batch effects significantly impact AI generalizability in prostate MRI, even among high-quality scans. Quantitative clustering enables detection of technical variations and supports diversity-aware training strategies that achieve equivalent performance with 2.3-fold fewer samples while eliminating batch effects.

SummaryAcquisition-related batch effects significantly impair AI generalizability in prostate MRI, even among scans meeting PI-QUAL quality standards. Clustering-based diversity-aware training strategies successfully eliminated these batch effects and achieved 2.23-fold greater training efficiency compared to single-site approaches, demonstrating that strategic technical diversity outweighs dataset size for developing robust, clinically deployable AI models.

Key PointsO_LIAcquisition-related batch effects significantly impair AI performance on prostate MRI, exceeding the impact of visual image quality as assessed by PI-QUAL scoring.
C_LIO_LIEven the model trained on the largest single cluster exhibited significant batch effects (p<0.001). In contrast, a balanced multi-cluster model eliminated cross-cluster variability (p=0.075) while maintaining equivalent performance and requiring a smaller sample size.
C_LIO_LIDiversity-aware training achieved 2.23-fold greater training efficiency (95% CI: 2.18-2.29) with 2.3-fold fewer samples, demonstrating that technical diversity outweighs data quantity for robust AI generalization.

Clinical relevanceAddressing batch effects is essential for developing reliable, generalizable AI tools for prostate MRI interpretation.

Disability is an important population-health concern, but adult-specific evidence on its distribution and socioeconomic patterning remains limited in Somaliland. This study estimated the prevalence and distribution of reported disability among adults in Somaliland and examined socioeconomic inequality, reported mental/psychological illness, and their co-occurrence.

We conducted a cross-sectional secondary analysis of the 2020 Somaliland Health and Demographic Survey. The analysis included 14,579 adults aged >18 years who were usual residents, had the disability module administered, and had a defined reported mental/psychological illness measure. Reported disability was defined as at least one positive response across seven disability domains: sight, hearing, speech, learning, mobility, self-care, and mental. Survey-weighted prevalence estimates and design-based comparisons were calculated. Survey-weighted logistic regression assessed associations with household wealth and other covariates. Socioeconomic inequality was assessed using a concentration index and the normalized Erreygers concentration index. Co-occurrence was evaluated by comparing observed joint prevalence with that expected under statistical independence and by survey-weighted logistic regression.

The survey-weighted prevalence of any reported disability was 7.30% (95% CI 6.65-8.02). Sight was the most frequently reported domain (3.83%, 95% CI 3.19-4.59), followed by hearing (1.54%, 95% CI 1.20-1.97) and mobility (1.39%, 95% CI 1.14-1.70). Disability prevalence increased markedly with age, from 4.15% among adults aged 18-29 years to 23.96% among those aged >60 years. The crude wealth pattern was non-monotonic and was not statistically detectable after adjustment for residence and region. The concentration index for reported disability was 0.0584 (SE 0.0284, p=0.0415). Reported mental/psychological illness had a weighted prevalence of 0.71% (95% CI 0.50-1.00). Both reported disability and reported mental/psychological illness occurred in 0.5032% of adults, compared with 0.05185% expected under statistical independence; the observed-to-expected ratio was 9.70 (95% CI 7.60-11.81). After adjustment for age group and sex, reported disability was strongly associated with reported mental/psychological illness (OR 42.99, 95% CI 18.45-100.18).

Reported disability affected approximately one in fourteen adults in Somaliland and showed a marked age gradient and substantial geographic variation. The crude socioeconomic pattern was attenuated after adjustment for geographic context, while concentration analysis indicated modest marginal concentration toward higher wealth ranks. Reported mental/psychological illness was uncommon but co-occurred with reported disability more often than expected under independence. These findings provide an adult population baseline for Somaliland while highlighting the need to distinguish survey-reported disability from the separate mental/psychological illness construct and to interpret the findings within the limitations of cross-sectional, survey-reported measures.

Author SummaryWhy was this study done? O_LIEvidence on disability among adults in Somaliland is limited, especially on its socioeconomic distribution and relationship with reported mental/psychological illness.
C_LIO_LIWe used the 2020 Somaliland Health and Demographic Survey to examine these patterns nationally.
C_LI What did the researchers do and find? O_LIWe analysed 14,579 adults aged 18 years or older using survey-weighted methods that accounted for the surveys sampling design.
C_LIO_LIOverall, 7.30% of adults reported at least one disability domain. Sight, hearing, and mobility were most frequently reported, and disability was much more common among older adults and varied across regions and residence settings.
C_LIO_LIReported mental/psychological illness was found in 0.71% of adults. Both conditions occurred together in 0.50%, substantially more than expected under statistical independence.
C_LI What do these findings mean? O_LIOur study provides an adult population baseline for reported disability in Somaliland and shows clear differences by age and geographic context.
C_LIO_LIOur findings highlight the importance of keeping reported disability and reported mental/psychological illness as distinct measures.
C_LIO_LIBecause our data are cross-sectional and based on reported survey measures, the findings describe the 2020 survey period and do not establish clinical diagnoses or causal relationships.

Background & AimsLanguage development in autism is heterogeneous and strongly predicts later functioning. The balance between receptive and expressive abilities and their developmental trajectories, however, remains poorly understood. While some autistic children exhibit a relative expressive advantage (ExpAdv), others show receptive advantage (RecAdv) or a balanced profile. Prior studies report inconsistent findings and are often limited by cross-sectional designs and small samples. The present study aimed to (1) describe longitudinal trajectories of receptive and expressive language in autistic and typically developing (TD) children; (2) classify children into ExpAdv, Balanced, and RecAdv profiles across early childhood; and (3) examine the stability and transitions of these profiles over time, including associated clinical features.

MethodsWe analyzed 1,174 longitudinal time points from 318 autistic children and 294 time points from 108 TD children (1.2-5.8 years) from the Geneva Autism Cohort. Receptive and expressive language were assessed with the Mullen Scales of Early Learning. Receptive-expressive balance was quantified as the ratio of receptive to expressive age equivalent scores, classifying children into ExpAdv, Balanced, and RecAdv profiles using adapted cut-offs. Mixed-effects models examined developmental trajectories, and Sankey diagrams visualized profile transitions. Autism features and adaptive behavior were compared across profiles.

ResultsAutistic children displayed lower expressive and receptive language than TD peers, with receptive abilities exceeding expressive skills in both groups. Overall, 30-35% of autistic children were classified as ExpAdv at 18-36 months, declining to [~]12% by 48-54 months, while Balanced and RecAdv profiles became more prevalent with age. ExpAdv was associated with slower verbal and non{-}verbal developmental gains. Balanced and RecAdv profiles showed moderate stability (50-60%), whereas ExpAdv was less stable and frequently transitioned toward Balanced profiles. Autistic children with stable ExpAdv profiles were more often female and showed weaker adaptive communication.

ConclusionsReceptive-expressive language profiles in autistic children are dynamic. ExpAdv profile is more frequent in younger autistic children, less stable, and linked to slower verbal and non-verbal development and greater autism severity.

ImplicationsExpAdv may represent an early marker of autism associated with slower expressive and receptive language growth. Longitudinal monitoring of receptive and expressive skills is essential, as transitions toward Balanced or RecAdv profiles are associated with improved developmental outcomes. We discuss clinical considerations regarding language assessment, longitudinal monitoring, and interpretation of receptive-expressive profiles.
observations.title: Longitudinal Receptive-Expressive Language Profiles in Young Autistic Children

metadata.summary: Nuclear receptor subfamily 4 group A member 2 (NR4A2) is a widely expressed immediate early gene induced by a host of physiological signals such as growth factors, cytokines, and neurotransmitters. In the adult mammalian heart, including in cardiomyocytes, NR4A2 mRNAs increase more than 60-fold in response to beta-adrenergic stimulation. However, the nature of the transcriptional remodeling induced by NR4A2 in the stressed heart has remained poorly investigated. We show here that NR4A2 activation in mouse cardiomyocytes leads to a rapid remodeling of the cardiac microRNA network. A total of 35 miRNAs were down-regulated, including the muscle-specific miR-133a and miR-499. On the opposite, 65 miRNAs were up-regulated, with a strong representation of miRNAs encoded within the imprinted Dlk1-Dio3 domain. Non-coding RNAs from the Dlk1-Dio3 locus are known for coordinating critical steps of cardiac development such as cardiac lineage commitment, cardiac morphogenesis, and cardiomyocyte proliferation, and for inhibiting mitochondrial function in myocytes. The findings shed light on a novel regulatory mechanism controlling cardiac homeostasis, and establish a framework to investigate further the roles played by NR4A2 in cardiac adaptation or maladaptation to various acute and pathological stress conditions.

observations.text: Computed tomography (CT) interpretation requires recognition of the anatomical level of each slice. Classification may facilitate preprocessing and AI-assisted fracture diagnosis. We developed deep learning models to classify craniofacial CT slices into six anatomical categories. A total of 11,769 images were collected from a multicenter database involving 10 Japanese university hospitals and the public Head-Neck-Radiomics-HN1 dataset. Patients were divided into training (70%) and evaluation (30%) sets. Five CNN architectures were trained from scratch, and hard- and soft-voting ensembles were evaluated. Individual-model accuracy ranged from 94.72% to 96.09%; the hard-voting ensemble achieved 96.46% accuracy (Cohens {kappa} = 0.954). Although performance differed among individual models (Cochrans Q = 99.29, p < 0.001), the ensemble did not significantly outperform EfficientNetV2B1 (McNemars p = 0.163). Errors occurred mainly between adjacent anatomical regions. Deep learning can classify craniofacial CT slices accurately and may support automated dataset organization and AI-assisted fracture diagnosis. External validation is needed.

metadata.summary: Degenerative mitral valve disease (DMVD) is a highly prevalent cardiac condition characterized by mitral valve interstitial cell (MVIC) activation and extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling. To investigate the transcriptional reprogramming underlying these processes, we performed RNA sequencing on an established three-dimensional (3D) porcine MVIC-collagen (VIC-COL) model.Following a 14-day maturation period, the constructs were treated with transforming growth factor-β1 (TGF-β1) for an additional 14 days, while untreated constructs cultured for the same duration served as controls. Samples were prepared from cells derived from three independent biological replicates (i.e. mitral valves from three different pigs). For each replicate, three constructs were pooled as one sample for final analysis. The analysis identified 915 differentially expressed genes (DEGs), revealing a significant transcriptional shift. Specifically, TGF-β1 led to a predominant upregulation of immune and inflammatory networks, including the IL-6/JAK/STAT3, TNF-α/NF-κB, and NOD-like receptor pathways, alongside processes associated with extracellular matrix organization, cell-cell adhesion, cell adhesion regulation, and cellular senescence. Furthermore, cross-species transcriptomic comparisons with a clinical canine DMVD dataset confirmed the conservation of these immune-centric signatures. Collectively, our findings suggest that immune-inflammatory signaling may act as a key modulator of ECM remodeling associated with MVIC activation. Moreover, the 3D VIC-COL system established in this study can serve as a reliable in vitro platform for investigating MVIC activation, ECM remodeling, and immune-related pathway changes in DMVD pathogenesis.

metadata.summary: Truncating variants in desmoplakin (DSP) are a leading cause of arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy, a severe heart muscle disease characterized by fibrosis and life-threatening arrhythmias. Desmoplakin anchors the junctions that hold heart muscle cells together to the internal cytoskeleton, enabling the heart to withstand the force of each contraction. No targeted therapy exists, and DSP is too large for conventional gene replacement. Here we show, in explanted human hearts and in human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes, that truncating DSP variants reduce desmoplakin RNA and protein, and that the resulting haploinsufficiency renders cardiomyocytes vulnerable to cell–cell adhesion failure under contractile stress, preceded by disruption of the cell membrane. Lowering contractile force with the myosin inhibitor mavacamten prevents this failure. Circumventing the size of DSP, CRISPR-based transcriptional activation of the endogenous gene restores desmoplakin expression and rescues adhesion. Haploinsufficiency is therefore the primary defect in DSP cardiomyopathy, and transcriptional activation offers a therapeutic strategy.

Background and AimsArtificial intelligence (AI) may help differentiate Takotsubo syndrome from acute anterior ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) on electrocardiograms (ECGs). We developed an ECG image-based model and evaluated whether AI assistance and visual explanations improved reader performance, overall and by reader background.

MethodsA self-supervised three-architecture deep learning ensemble was developed and externally validated using 12-lead ECG images from two institutions, recorded [≤]14 days after onset regardless of reperfusion. A four-phase reader study compared unaided interpretation, a reference sheet, and AI assistance (Phases 1-3). In Phase 4, readers were randomized to the reference sheet alone, AI predictions, or predictions with gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM). Correctness was analyzed with generalized linear mixed-effects models.

ResultsCohorts comprised 832 development and 95 external validation participants. External validation accuracy was 0.914, and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.970 (95% CI, 0.938-0.992), or 0.958 using first recorded ECGs. Among 70 readers, the estimated probability of correct diagnosis increased from 0.632 unaided to 0.864 with AI (odds ratio [OR], 3.71; P<0.001). In Phase 4, AI assistance improved accuracy vs reference sheet (OR, 4.28; 95% CI, 3.08-5.95), and Grad-CAM added value (OR, 1.53; 95% CI, 1.04-2.25). In exploratory analyses, less experienced readers gained more; with AI, non-cardiologists outperformed cardiologists. Mean AI-assisted reader accuracy remained below model accuracy.

ConclusionsAn ECG image-based ensemble differentiated Takotsubo syndrome from anterior STEMI and improved reader performance, particularly with visual explanations. Experience-related differences emphasize the need for effective human-AI interaction.

Key FindingIn external validation, the ensemble achieved 0.914 accuracy and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.970. Among 70 readers, AI assistance improved accuracy (randomized Phase 4 odds ratio 4.28), and heatmap explanations added benefit (odds ratio 1.53).

metadata.summary: Bulk RNA sequencing was performed to assess transcriptional responses to PD173952 in cultured primary mouse cardiac fibroblasts and human pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes. Primary mouse cardiac fibroblasts were analyzed under three conditions: vehicle (DMSO), TGF-beta stimulation, and TGF-beta stimulation with PD173952 treatment. Fibroblasts were treated with TGF-beta for 48 h, and PD173952 or vehicle was added during the final 24 h before RNA extraction. hPSC-derived cardiomyocytes were analyzed after 24 h treatment with PD173952 or vehicle (DMSO). This dataset was generated to examine the effects of PD173952 on profibrotic transcriptional responses in fibroblasts and on cardiomyocyte transcriptional programs in a human in vitro model.

observations.text: Neuroanatomical pathways link specialized brain regions, but whether regional transcriptomic profiles preserve relationships aligned with pathway order remains unclear. We defined candidate pathways and their available tissue representations from neuroanatomical literature, then screened 10,262 genes in the Body Index of Gene Expression (BIGE), a human microarray resource covering cells and tissues. The screen required expression across every mapped region of a route and limited single-region dominance. It identified 23 candidates in three routes with sufficient coverage; 19 met the criteria for the dorsal column-medial lemniscus (DCML) representation and formed the fixed panel. We evaluated this panel in six Allen Human Brain Atlas (AHBA) donors across three central regional representations: an aggregate of samples assigned to the cuneate and gracile nuclei (Cu/Gr), the lateral group of nuclei, ventral division, within the dorsal thalamus (DTLv), and postcentral gyrus. The regional-order contrast compared the mean similarity of the pairs adjacent in the anatomical sequence, Cu/Gr-DTLv and DTLv-postcentral gyrus, with Cu/Gr-postcentral gyrus similarity. Both adjacent-in-order correlations were positive in all six donors; the contrast was positive in five and reached a mean of T = 0.345175 (exact sign test, P = 0.109375). The panel exceeded two distributions of 50,000 gene sets generated under comparable selection constraints (P = 0.027919 and P = 0.026579). In descriptive anatomical comparisons, it ranked third among 240 combinations and first among the target and all 16 single-region substitutions. All 50,000 one-probe-per-gene analyses retained T > 0, and broad neuronal-expression contrasts were positive in medulla, thalamus, and cortex. Spatial support depended on the null model, with stronger evidence under whole-donor surrogates (P = 0.003860) than under the primary within-compartment model (P = 0.051179). These findings identify a fixed gene panel whose regional similarity is aligned with the represented central order of the DCML system and define a specific hypothesis for prospective evaluation in an independent, anatomically resolved dataset.
observations.title: An anatomy-constrained transcriptomic screen identifies a 19-gene panel with an ordered regional similarity pattern in the human somatosensory system
